Amber
ăm´bĕr
n. (the glowing metallic colour at the centre of Ezekiel's visions of the glory; Hebrew chashmal)
Through French from Arabic anbar. The KJV uses it for Hebrew chashmal, a word found only in Ezekiel — a bright burnished alloy glowing like fire, rendered electrum in the Greek.

Biblical Definition

Amber in Scripture is never a stone and never an ornament; it is the colour of the glory. At the opening of the visions: “out of the midst thereof as the colour of amber, out of the midst of the fire” (Eze 1:4). At the centre of the throne: “And I saw as the colour of amber, as the appearance of fire round about within it” (Eze 1:27). And again when the prophet is carried to Jerusalem: “as the appearance of brightness, as the colour of amber” (Eze 8:2). Ezekiel piles up as and appearance and likeness because he is describing what cannot be described, and he ends where the whole vision was going: “This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD. And when I saw it, I fell upon my face” (Eze 1:28).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines amber as a hard, semi-pellucid substance, tasteless and without smell except when heated, of a yellowish colour, susceptible of a fine polish.

expand to see more

AMBER, n. A hard semi-pellucid substance, tasteless and without smell, except when pounded or heated, when it emits a fragrant odor. It is found in alluvial soils, or on the sea shore.

AMBER, a. Consisting of amber; resembling amber; as an amber-colored liquor.

Key Scripture

Eze 1:4 — "And I looked, and, behold, a whirlwind came out of the north, a great cloud, and a fire infolding itself, and a brightness was about it, and out of the midst thereof as the colour of amber, out of the midst of the fire."

Eze 1:27 — "And I saw as the colour of amber, as the appearance of fire round about within it, from the appearance of his loins even upward, and from the appearance of his loins even downward, I saw as it were the appearance of fire, and it had brightness round about."

Eze 8:2 — "Then I beheld, and lo a likeness as the appearance of fire: from the appearance of his loins even downward, fire; and from his loins even upward, as the appearance of brightness, as the colour of amber."

Eze 1:28 — "As the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud in the day of rain, so was the appearance of the brightness round about. This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD. And when I saw it, I fell upon my face, and I heard a voice of one that spake."

Modern Corruption

Ezekiel's hedged language is reverence, not vagueness, and the right response to the glory is the one he gives: he fell on his face.

expand to see more

The chain of qualifiers in Ezekiel 1 — the appearance of the likeness of the glory — is often read as though the prophet were unsure of what he saw. He was not. He was certain of what he saw and certain that human speech could not carry it, and so he laid one comparison on another and refused to say that any of them was the thing itself. This is the creaturely reserve that the second commandment protects. God may show His glory; man may not fix it in an image. Ezekiel gives us colour and fire and a bow in the cloud, and then he gives us his face on the ground.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the vision ends in worship and not in curiosity. There is a long tradition of mining Ezekiel 1 for a diagram — the wheels, the faces, the amber all charted, dated, and assigned — and a shorter modern one of mining it for spectacle. Both stop where Ezekiel does not stop. The prophet who saw the throne fell on his face and then heard a voice, and the voice sent him to preach to a rebellious house. Glory seen and not obeyed has been misread.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew chashmal (H2830), a glowing brightness or burnished metal, only in Ezekiel; kabod (H3519), glory, weight; nogah (H5051), brightness.

expand to see more

Hebrew chashmal (H2830) — amber, glowing metal; Ezekiel 1:4, 1:27, 8:2 only.

Hebrew kabod (H3519) — glory, weight, honour; Ezekiel 1:28, Exodus 33:18, Isaiah 6:3.

Hebrew nogah (H5051) — brightness, shining; Ezekiel 1:4, 1:27, Habakkuk 3:4.

Hebrew demuth (H1823) — likeness, similitude; Ezekiel 1:5, 1:28, Genesis 1:26.

Hebrew mareh (H4758) — appearance, vision; Ezekiel 1:27, 1:28, Numbers 12:8.

Usage

"“As the colour of amber, out of the midst of the fire” — the glory at the storm's centre."

"“The appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD” — reverence in the grammar."

"“And when I saw it, I fell upon my face” — the only fit response."
